note: Artifacts too large for git. Fetch with scripts/fetch_models.py. The small heads trained on top of these -- models/frame_aligner.pt (2.2 MB), models/tone_sequence.pt (1.1 MB) and models/gop_reference_neural.json -- live in the repository instead, so a clone gets sub-second alignment and the better tone reading with no fetch step. The calibration files committed in models/ (gop_reference.json, word_duration_stats.json) are measurements of THIS acoustic model's behaviour and are wrong for any other -- see acoustic_model_sha256. gop_reference_neural.json is the same measurement for the neural aligner, whose scores are log-posteriors rather than GMM log-likelihoods and are not on the same scale.

models/yoruba_acoustic.zip.purpose: MFA acoustic model, trained on 193,309 utterances from 2,801 speakers (~118 h: SLR86, studio corpus, YECS). Everything else is calibrated against it.

models/vowel_classifier.joblib.purpose: Vowel identity, 393,534 vowels from 903 speakers, fitted to models/finetuned_utterance over neural-aligner spans -- the spans the engine produces, rather than MFA's. Carries a syllabic-nasal class (n~) the previous model lacked. It names its encoder and its labels in the bundle and the engine reads both, so neither the pair nor the class order can drift.

models/tone_classifier.joblib.purpose: Fallback tone classifier: a gradient-boosted tree over 14 pitch features, 205,690 vowels from 2,702 speakers. Superseded by models/tone_sequence.pt, which reads a whole utterance at once and is committed to git rather than released because it is 1.1 MB. On one identical held-out set the sequence model scores 74.7%, this tree 69.0%, the 36-speaker tree it replaces 66.6%, and the threshold rules 56.3%.

models/finetuned_utterance/model.safeten.purpose: The encoder the vowel classifier is fitted to. LyngualLabs' mms-300m-yoruba-english fine-tuned on whole utterances and truncated to the 16 layers the engine reads. Required: the classifier reads noise from any other encoder.

vowel_classifier.caveat: Held-out composition changed between versions as more speakers entered the corpus, so figures are comparable only within a controlled comparison.

controlled_comparison.note: Identical rows, identical classifier, identical speaker split.

corpora: studio corpus (michsethowusu, Waxal, IroyinSpeech, Common Voice 26.0, ljspeech, thisniyi)

models/whisper-yoruba.purpose: Whisper checkpoint for open-vocabulary transcription. Optional only in the sense that the engine runs without it: without a recogniser the learner's transcript is the prompt echoed back, so the word table cannot name a substituted word and verification falls back to alignment coverage, a proxy that reaches 72% balanced accuracy. Fetch it with --include-optional if you are serving the app.
